A living landscape at the beginning

THIS IS WHERE
IT BEGINS.

140 hectares of Mediterranean land — not presented as finished, but opened as a place to observe, learn, restore and build with care.

Monte Ventosa is becoming one of the first living project grounds connected to Terra-Be-Utopia: a place where regeneration can be explored in real soil, real water, real buildings and real life.

A living vision taking shape

A landscape where possibility becomes real.

Monte Ventosa is a 140-hectare rural landscape in Portugal’s Alentejo — with old structures, open land, trees, water and the beginnings of cultivation.

That unfinished quality is part of its value. Instead of arriving after every decision has been made, teachers, learners, practitioners and partners can encounter a real place while its regenerative direction is still taking shape.

The vision is already here. How it takes shape will grow from the land itself — by listening first, working with what is here, and allowing something beautiful, useful and regenerative to emerge.

What can grow here

A place for land, learning, restoration — and life.

Monte Ventosa is envisioned as a regenerative living landscape: not one single programme and not one model of community, but a place where ecological restoration, practical skills, personal growth and everyday life can exist side by side.

Land & Water

Permaculture, water retention, soil regeneration, Mediterranean planting, syntropic systems, food forests and long-term observation.

Farm-to-Table

Food Craft · Homesteading · Self-Sufficiency
From growing and harvesting to processing and preserving: future gardens and orchards, eggs and other foods from our own animals, olive oil production, sourdough and wood-fired baking, cheese making, fermentation, food preservation, wild herbs, natural soap making and other traditional skills that reconnect everyday life with the land.

Natural Building

Restoring existing structures and exploring earth, lime, natural materials and climate-appropriate building.

Nature Spa & Water

Outdoor spaces for rest and reconnection, including the future vision of a natural swimming lagoon or pool integrated into the landscape.

Off-Grid & Co-Living

Simple, lower-impact living with private space, optional shared activities and future areas for longer stays, remote work and digital nomads.

Workshops & Skills

Pottery, natural building, food skills, sourdough days, forest-bathing days, nature connection and practical learning experiences.

Children & Wilderness Learning

Long-term, wilderness-education-inspired projects where children can explore, build, create, learn practical skills and share real adventures while parents attend a course, help on site or simply stay at Monte Ventosa.

Inner Regeneration

Grounding, breath, intention, nervous-system regulation, embodiment and practices that support reconnection with oneself and the natural world.

Space to Belong — and Retreat

Connection without constant togetherness: shared experiences when desired, and enough private space to rest, create, work and simply be.

Come close to the process

You do not have to wait until it is finished.

Some people will first meet Monte Ventosa through a course. Others may come to help prepare the site, support an event, share expertise, test useful equipment or collaborate on one part of the wider regenerative work.

The aim is not constant togetherness. Monte Ventosa is imagined as a co-living landscape where privacy, autonomy and shared responsibility can coexist. Everyone who lives here is invited to take responsibility for particular areas of everyday life and to care for them with independence and commitment — while always being free to join forces, share knowledge and tend to things together.

At its heart is a simple idea: to take responsibility for ourselves, for one another and for the living world around us. To rediscover something villages once understood naturally — that we can have our own space and still look out for one another, contribute to something larger than ourselves and know that we do not have to carry everything alone.

Follow the journey

Stay close as Monte Ventosa unfolds.

Not everyone who feels connected to the vision needs to take part right away. Our newsletter is a quiet way to follow what is taking shape here — new courses and workshops, seasonal projects, volunteer opportunities, stories from the land and the small steps that gradually turn the vision into reality.
